kind: PRODUCT fix for phase 12's remaining two confirmed MAJORs, both in conductor_setup, plus one row owed by C-087. Each was REPRODUCED BY RUNNING by the gate's adjudicator against the real handleSetup, not inferred. Both leave the operator with a repo that reports success and cannot work.
authoredBy: orchestrator — authored from docs/build/artifacts/phase-gates-12-13-15-findings.md phase 12 MAJORs 5 and 6, with the adjudicator's measured outputs quoted verbatim below.
bindings: Repairs assertion rows 12.2-proofs-origin-fail-soft and 12.2-detect-multi-ecosystem, and pins the untested --print-env behaviour change C-087 recorded. Phase 12's gate stays FAIL until MAJOR 1 (G5 equivalence) is also closed.
verifiedAgainstHead: MAJOR 5 — conductor/adapter/tools.ts:8564. setupProofRequest's guard is `if (result !== null || input.failoverState.useUpstream) return result;`. Every concurrent request that RESUMES AFTER the first failover therefore returns null instead of retrying the upstream, so one router outage during the maxReaders-wide fan-out is misreported as a slot shortage.

MAJOR 5 MEASURED against the real handleSetup with two stub origins, where the router answers GET /v1/models and the schema probe then refuses every later connection — exactly what the 12.1 supervisor's restart window looks like. All six slot probes are issued together and all six fail at the router; the first continuation to resume latches useUpstream and retries the upstream successfully; the other five see useUpstream already true and return null WITHOUT EVER TOUCHING the healthy upstream. Result: `ok:false`, `written:false`, `upstream saw: ["POST /v1/chat/completions"]` — 1 of 6 — and the failure text 'of 6 concurrent readers the served origin held only 1 open ... Remedy: restart llama-server with --parallel 6, and raise --ctx-size with it'.

MAJOR 5's remedy is wrong in every particular: llama-server was healthy with six slots, and the operator is left unconfigured. Row 12.2-proofs-origin-fail-soft states 'a DOWN router is never itself a setup failure ... Setup fails only on what the proofs themselves prove false'.

MAJOR 5's coverage gap has a specific cause: the CONTROL run (router dead from the very first proof) returns ok:true, because the sequential /v1/models proof latches useUpstream BEFORE the fan-out. That ordering is the only reason the committed 12.2-proofs-origin-fail-soft test is green — the concurrent leg is untested.

MAJOR 5's suggested fix, from the adjudicator: drop `|| input.failoverState.useUpstream` from :8564 and rely on the `second === first` check at :8580. With that change the reproduction reports ok:true AND `bash scripts/test-conductor.sh` stays green — which is itself the proof that no existing test covers this leg.

MAJOR 6 — conductor/adapter/tools.ts:8422. setupRequiredScopes returns `[]` for zero detected ecosystems and handleSetup has NO coverage guard, so the empty array is written. Row 12.2-detect-multi-ecosystem states 'requiredScopes is never written as an empty array (which would validate cleanly while leaving every path unverified)' — the exact state produced.

MAJOR 6 zero-ecosystem MEASURED: on a git repo holding only README.md and a Makefile, handleSetup returned ok:true, written:true, failures:[], and the written .conductor/config.json carried `verify.scopes {}` and `verify.requiredScopes []`, with `validate("Config", written).ok === true` because core/types.ts declares no minItems/minProperties.

MAJOR 6's consequence is a WEDGED REPO THAT REPORTED SUCCESS: repoConfigured flips true and gates-phase opens every gate, but every item afterwards throws at tools.ts:2716 ('no verify.requiredScopes entry covers item ...') on submit_test, vet_test, mark_green and item_review — and setup is then ILLEGAL TO RE-RUN without reconfigure:true (tools.ts:8853).

MAJOR 6 multi-ecosystem MEASURED: each entry's pattern is that ecosystem's extension glob, so every non-source path is covered by none of them. With the two globs setupRequiredScopes emits for package.json + CMakeLists.txt, `globMatch` is FALSE for README.md, docs/guide.md, CMakeLists.txt, package.json and scripts/build.sh against BOTH patterns (src/app.ts matches node only, src/main.cpp cmake only). The SINGLE-ecosystem branch writes '**' and has no hole at all.
MAJOR 6's downstream victim is first-class: a docs-only item — the shape conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts scenario 4 treats as legitimate — throws at tools.ts:2716, and conductor_report throws at 7542.

MAJOR 6's coverage gap has a specific cause: setup.test.ts:965-971 samples only src/a.js, lib/util.js, test/util.test.js, src/main.cpp and include/x.hpp — exactly the covered set, and none of the uncovered ones.

C-087's owed row — scripts/serve.py's `--print-env` now routes around choose_model and, with no model in argv and none in the saved session, exits NON-ZERO with a stderr error instead of opening an interactive picker. Correct for a reporting flag (choose_model writes its list to stdout with info() and blocks on 'Select a model by number', violating both --print-env properties through a second door), but currently pinned by nothing.
specGaps: P12B-SG-1 (MAJOR 5's fix must not resurrect the thundering herd). The `useUpstream` latch exists so that N concurrent readers do not each independently re-probe a dead router. Removing the guard outright must not mean every one of the six retries the router first. RESOLUTION: a request that resumes after the latch is already set must go STRAIGHT to the upstream — it must not return null, and it must not re-probe the router. The `second === first` check at :8580 remains the equality proof.

P12B-SG-2 (MAJOR 6's zero-ecosystem answer is a REFUSAL, not a fabricated scope). Setup must not invent a verify command for a repo it cannot characterise. RESOLUTION: writing an empty requiredScopes is forbidden; the honest outcomes are to refuse with a message naming what it could not detect, or to write a coverage entry the operator is told to complete. What is NOT acceptable is ok:true with a config that wedges every later item.

P12B-SG-3 (MAJOR 6's multi-ecosystem answer must cover the whole tree). The single-ecosystem branch already writes '**' and has no hole; the multi branch must likewise leave no path uncovered. Whether that is a trailing '**' catch-all entry or a widened per-ecosystem pattern is implementation freedom — the row asserts coverage, not shape.
P12B-SG-4 (out of scope). MAJOR 1 (G5 equivalence) is separate work. The four recorded MINORs are not in scope. Do not touch the C++ router.

assertions.text: a router that dies DURING the concurrent slot fan-out is not a setup failure: with an origin that answers the sequential proofs and then refuses every later connection, all maxReaders concurrent probes reach the healthy upstream — the upstream sees ALL of them, not 1 of 6 — and setup returns ok:true and writes its config. Asserted on what the UPSTREAM received, because that is the fact the defect destroyed; the measured failure was `upstream saw: ["POST /v1/chat/completions"]` with five requests silently returning null

the test drives the CONCURRENT leg specifically, not the control the committed test already covers: the router must survive the sequential /v1/models proof and die only afterwards, because a router dead from the first proof latches useUpstream BEFORE the fan-out and returns ok:true even at HEAD. That ordering is the entire reason the existing 12.2-proofs-origin-fail-soft test is green over this defect, so a new test that does not pin the ordering repeats the same blind spot

the fix does not resurrect the thundering herd the latch exists to prevent (P12B-SG-1): once the latch is set, later requests go STRAIGHT to the upstream — they do not each re-probe the dead router. Asserted by counting what the DEAD origin received across the fan-out, so a fix that simply deleted the latch fails this row while satisfying the one above

on a repo setup cannot characterise — the measured case is a git repo holding only README.md and a Makefile — setup NEVER writes `requiredScopes: []`. Either it refuses with a message naming what it could not detect, or it writes coverage an operator is told to complete; what it may not do is return ok:true with a config that validates cleanly and then throws at every submit_test, vet_test, mark_green and item_review while being illegal to re-run without reconfigure:true

with two or more ecosystems detected, EVERY path in the repo is covered by some requiredScopes entry — asserted with the exact paths measured as uncovered: README.md, docs/guide.md, CMakeLists.txt, package.json and scripts/build.sh, each of which returned false against BOTH emitted globs. The single-ecosystem branch already writes '**' and has no hole; this row makes the multi branch match that guarantee

the downstream consequence is gone, proved end to end rather than at the glob: after a multi-ecosystem setup, a docs-only item — the shape e2e scenario 4 treats as first-class — does NOT throw 'no verify.requiredScopes entry covers item' at tools.ts:2716, and conductor_report does not throw at 7542. A coverage fix that satisfied globMatch but left the handler throwing would pass the row above and still leave the repo unusable

the C-087 behaviour change is pinned: `--print-env` with no model in argv and none in the saved session exits NON-ZERO with a message on STDERR naming why, and never opens the interactive picker — choose_model writes its list to stdout with info() and blocks on 'Select a model by number', which violates both properties --print-env promises, through a second door from the port resolution already fixed
